about.title: About Mutual Fund Calculator - Investment Growth Analysis Tool
about.description: The Mutual Fund Calculator is a comprehensive investment analysis tool designed to help you calculate potential returns, growth projections, and costs associated with mutual fund investments. This calculator analyzes initial investments, monthly contributions, expected returns, and fees to project long-term wealth building through mutual funds. Whether you're planning retirement savings or building investment portfolios, this tool provides accurate mutual fund growth calculations.

faq.q: What's a reasonable expected return for mutual funds?
faq.a: Historically, diversified stock mutual funds have averaged 7-10% annually over long periods. Bond funds typically return 3-6%. Conservative balanced funds might return 5-8%. Use historical averages but remember past performance doesn't guarantee future results.

faq.q: How do mutual fund fees affect my returns?
faq.a: Expense ratios significantly impact long-term returns. A 1% difference in fees can cost tens of thousands over decades. For example, 0.5% vs. 1.5% expense ratios on a $100,000 investment can differ by $50,000+ over 30 years.

faq.q: Should I invest a lump sum or monthly amounts?
faq.a: Both strategies work well. Lump sum investing historically performs better due to more time in market, but dollar-cost averaging through monthly investments reduces timing risk and helps build consistent investing habits.

faq.q: What types of mutual funds should I consider?
faq.a: Consider your risk tolerance and timeline. Stock funds for long-term growth, bond funds for stability, balanced funds for moderate risk, and target-date funds for automatic diversification. International funds add geographic diversification.
